title: Pure grade spans and joint conservativity in finite filtered presentations
statement: Let C be abelian and P a finite filtered bounded-below derived presentation on a triangulated category D [def-trf-finite-filtered-derived-presentation]. For each p there are endofunctors cut and piece and natural arrows M→cut(M)←piece(M). All grades of cut(M) above p vanish; piece(M) is pure of grade p; if M is pure of grade p, so is cut(M). The first arrow is universal for maps into objects with no grades above p, and the second is universal for maps out of objects with no grades below p. For every exact functor H from D to another such presentation, preserving each finite filtration interval, both arrows become isomorphisms after H followed by the pth graded functor. This is the structure Presentation.GradedSpan P p, and it is nonempty. Moreover if every grade of M vanishes, M is zero.

source.place: §§5.1.1(b)–(e), 5.1.2(a)–(c), and the cutoff argument of Lemma 5.1.4(i), pp.39–41

proof.text: Represent M by a uniformly finite filtered complex K. Its filtration bounds show finite graded support: below the lower bound the inclusion of consecutive steps is invertible, and above the upper bound the quotient is zero. If all grades of M vanish, K→0 is a graded quasi-isomorphism, since the graded comparison identifies its image with a map of zero objects. Localization inverts it. A localization preserves a zero object: lift the unique incoming and outgoing natural transformations and use naturality at that object to prove uniqueness of all maps. Thus grades jointly detect zero objects.

source.place: §§5.1.1(b)–(e), 5.1.2(a)–(c), and the cutoff argument of Lemma 5.1.4(i), pp.39–41

proof.text: Obtain high and low with their universal maps from the presentation truncation theorem. Complete high(r)M→M to a distinguished triangle with cone Z. The retained-grade isomorphisms show Z is low-supported. Universality factors M→Z through low(r)M. The resulting low(r)M→Z is an isomorphism on every grade, using the two zero-vertex criteria and the low grade maps. Its cone is zero by the previous step. Transport this triangle along that isomorphism to get a cutoff triangle.

source.place: §§5.1.1(b)–(e), 5.1.2(a)–(c), and the cutoff argument of Lemma 5.1.4(i), pp.39–41

proof.text: Set cut=low(p+1) and piece=cut followed by high(p); the support formulas give the stated purity and the universal properties are the two Hom bijections. An interval-preserving functor preserves high and low support, because every input has finite support at the other end. Apply H followed by grade p to the cutoff triangles at p+1 and p. The discarded vertices vanish, so the quotient and inclusion respectively become invertible.

theorem Presentation.truncationSpans (P : Presentation (C := C) (D := D)) :
    (∀ p : ℤ, Nonempty (P.GradedSpan p)) ∧
    (∀ M : D, (∀ p : ℤ, IsZero ((P.gr p).obj M)) → IsZero M)
